steps.tx: Microscopic evaluation of urinary sediment provides an essential non-invasive window into renal parenchymal integrity. **Acanthocytes**, defined as ring-shaped red cells with blebs or vesicle projections, strongly establish active **glomerular haematuria** when they exceed **5%** of excreted red blood cells. Similarly, genuine **red blood cell casts** establish capillary wall disruption in acute glomerulonephritis, distinguishing glomerular bleeding from lower tract urological sources.

steps.tx: Urinary casts form exclusively within distal tubular lumens. **Muddy brown granular casts** consist of sloughed necrotic tubular epithelial cells embedded in a **Tamm-Horsfall** mucoprotein matrix. Their presence confirms the diagnosis of **acute tubular necrosis** in acute kidney injury. In contrast, **broad waxy casts** with blunt fractured ends signify marked tubular dilation and stasis characteristic of advanced **chronic kidney disease**.

left.title: Acute Tubular Necrosis
points: Cast type: Muddy brown granular casts
Significance: Active ischemic or toxic damage

right.title: Advanced CKD
points: Pathology: Marked tubular dilation and atrophy
Cast type: Broad waxy casts with fractured ends
Significance: Severe nephron loss and stasis

steps.tx: Standard **dipstick protein** detection relies on colorimetric dye binding with **tetrabromphenol blue**. This reagent is sensitive primarily to negatively charged albumin but fails to detect low concentrations of immunoglobulin light chains, termed **Bence Jones** proteinuria, or tubular microproteins. Sulfosalicylic acid precipitation testing is mandatory whenever light chain excretion is suspected clinically.

steps.tx: Quantitative staging of **albuminuria** relies on the spot **urine albumin-to-creatinine ratio**, abbreviated as **ACR**. Staging classifies excretion into category A1, denoting normal to mildly increased excretion under **30** mg/g; category A2, denoting moderately increased excretion between **30** and **300** mg/g; and category A3, signifying severely increased excretion exceeding **300** mg/g.

steps.tx: **Orthostatic proteinuria**, or postural proteinuria, represents a benign condition present exclusively during upright posture and completely absent in first-morning **recumbent** urine samples. Total protein excretion typically remains under **1** g per day in young adults. Demonstrating normal protein excretion in recumbent first-morning samples confirms the diagnosis and avoids unnecessary invasive renal biopsies.

steps.tx: **Tubular proteinuria** develops when proximal tubular injury impairs receptor-mediated endocytosis of freely filtered low-molecular-weight proteins. Patients excrete **beta-2 microglobulin**, alpha-1 microglobulin, and **retinol-binding protein** without nephrotic-range albuminuria. This distinctive pattern confirms tubulointerstitial disease, heavy metal nephrotoxicity, or Fanconi syndrome rather than glomerular filtration barrier disruption.

left.title: Glomerular Proteinuria
points: Pathology: Barrier pore defect and charge loss
Clinical range: Frequently reaches nephrotic levels

right.title: Tubular Proteinuria
points: Primary proteins: Beta-2 microglobulin and retinol-binding protein
Clinical range: Mild proteinuria below nephrotic range

steps.tx: Microscopic crystal analysis identifies metabolic stones and acute nephrotoxins. Acidic urine reveals envelope-shaped **calcium oxalate** dihydrate crystals or dumbbell monohydrate crystals in **ethylene glycol** toxicity. In contrast, alkaline urine with urease-producing bacteria yields coffin-lid **magnesium ammonium phosphate** crystals, confirming struvite infection calculus formation.
